<thought>We need the predefined isotopic distributions to compare with the observed pattern and determine which elements have distinctive signatures present in the spectrum. The observed spectrum shows a series of peaks spaced ~1 Da with rapidly decreasing intensity, which matches the natural isotopic pattern of carbon (C‑12 dominant, C‑13 ~1.1 % per carbon). This pattern alone indicates the presence of carbon. No other element in the provided list (Cl, Br, S, etc.) shows a series of many peaks; they show one or two characteristic peaks. Therefore, the only element that can be definitively identified from the isotope distribution is carbon.</thought>
<final_answer>['C']</final_answer>
